messages:
sam_h: Heads-up — spotted a regression in expert routing perf on the 64k-token benchmark after the kernel-selector change. p50 token latency up ~12%, GPU-side stall time looks like comm waiting. :frowning:
maya: ugh. can you paste the traces?
sam_h: gist of the perf capture below. ran `nsys` across 8 GPUs (tp=2, pp=2, experts sharded). main symptom: repeated `ncclAllToAll` calls with long tail (~4-6ms) every routing step. compute kernels are 0.8-1.2ms but stalls between them.
---
perfbot: [auto-trace] https://perf.internal/redwood/trace/1858204321 (nvtx + nccl timeline attached)
---
ravi: that nccl tail rings a bell — recent NCCL upgrade changed algorithms for small messages. could be falling back to an algorithm that uses more eager buffer transfers. did you repro with NCCL_ASYNCERROR=INFO?
sam_h: repro with NCCL v2.18.5 and 2.19.0. both show tails but 2.19 slightly worse. setting NCCL_DEBUG=INFO shows frequent `alltoall` chunking into many small sends.
maya: what's the routing fanout distribution? are many tokens hitting the same expert set and causing imbalanced messages?
sam_h: distribution is relatively flat, but we pushed an optimization to pack per-expert requests into `group_size=16` blocks. that changed the shape: fewer huge messages, more medium-sized ones, which seems to interact badly with NCCL for our interconnect (DGX A100 NVLink mesh).
carla: can you paste the batching config? maybe we can tune `pack_threshold` or fall back to a per-GPU fuse buffer.
sam_h: config snippet: ```
# routing config
pack_threshold: 16
max_group_bytes: 128k
batch_timeout_ms: 3
````
carla: try increasing `max_group_bytes` to 512k or raising `batch_timeout_ms` to 6ms to create fewer, larger messages. measured tradeoffs: slightly higher latency per routing hop but much lower all-to-all overhead overall.
ravi: also consider enabling NCCL_RING_THRESHOLD or force `NCCL_TOPO_FILE`-guided algorithm to prefer 2-step reduce-scatter + allgather instead of direct alltoall for our mesh. that often improves overlap with compute.
maya: do we have comm/compute overlap enabled? runtime should issue async send/recv and launch compute while waiting, but the routing code may be serializing.
sam_h: yeah, we found a serialization point in the KV cache apply path — we were doing a blocking memcpy into the fused comm buffer before launching the kernel. fixing to async `cudaMemcpyAsync` + stream ordering cuts 30% of the stall window in local test.
carla: nice. can you add a diff to the PR and perfbot run?
sam_h: will do. small patch preview: ```diff
- memcpy(host_buf, gpu_buf, n);
- ncclAllToAll(...);
+ cudaMemcpyAsync(comm_buf, gpu_buf, n, cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice, comm_stream);
+ ncclGroupStart();
+ ncclAllToAll(..., comm_stream);
+ ncclGroupEnd();
```
perfbot: queued distributed perf run with that patch: run_id=2026-03-18-398. baseline vs patch in ~30m.
ravi: if async memcpy helps, also ensure kernel selection doesn't pull compute onto the same stream as comm. we should separate compute_stream and comm_stream and use event-based sync only when necessary. recent kernel-selector change colocated small kernels on default stream which could block comm.
maya: good catch. that explains why some of the short kernels (kernel selection, kv-apply) pushed onto default stream are causing extra serialization.
sam_h: another observation: p99 alltoall latency correlates with nvlink utilization spikes + CPU thread that polls NCCL being pinned to a hot core. moving NCCL polling thread to a less noisy core lowered variance.
carla: can you share `nvidia-smi topo -m` and the pinned core? also we should test with `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` to confirm it's NVLink vs IB.
sam_h: added outputs in perf gist. tested NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 — tail improved slightly, but not eliminated. looks NVLink scheduling + algorithm choice.
ravi: roadmap: 1) land async memcpy + stream separation 2) increase pack sizes as fallback 3) experiment with forcing algorithm via `NCCL_ALGO` and topo-guided `NCCL_TOPO_FILE` 4) add telemetry for per-hop alltoall size histogram so we can detect pathological packing automatically.
maya: agreed. also add a short-lived canary job on Dedicated which simulates our real traffic — prod-like topology matters.
carla: will add an alert rule: if >30% of routing calls have <1KB payload and variance in alltoall latency > 2x baseline, page eng-runtime.
sam_h: thanks. I'll open PRs: one for async memcpy + stream split, one for batching knob defaults, and a telemetry task. assigning: sam_h -> PRs, carla -> alert + telemetry schema, ravi -> NCCL experiment. I'll post links when ready. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy queued to canary pool (canary-3) for perf run id=2026-03-18-398.
perfbot: perf run complete. summary: async memcpy + stream split reduces mean routing stall 28%, end-to-end token latency p50 down 8%, p99 down 18%. collecting full flamegraph now.
sam_h: awesome. closing this thread and moving tasks to cards.
